composition.serve_who: This sheet is the "230V AC AFT DISTRIBUTION PANEL" (GMMS 108'-102a) — a 230V AC sub-distribution board serving the AFT half of the vessel: AFT OUTLETS, GALLEY 1 and GALLEY 2 supply lines, each protected by its own earth-leakage (RCD) relay, feeding a bank of 17 branch breakers (Q1-Q17). Each breaker's downstream load-name identifies the equipment it serves (galley appliances, wine cooler, outlets zones, induction hob). This is a distribution/infrastructure sheet: individual equipment nodes get their supply fact; the panel/bus/earth-leakage structure itself is infrastructure belonging to this AFT distribution panel (no dedicated panel node exists in the register — recorded as infrastructure with no fitting node beyond noting it here).

infrastructure.system_name: 230V AC AFT Distribution Panel — bus/earth-leakage structure
facts: Panel titled '230V AC AFT DISTRIBUTION PANEL', drawing GMMS 108'-102a; no dedicated distribution-panel node exists in the register — recorded as infrastructure with no fitting node.
Three incoming feeds, each behind its own earth-leakage (RCD) relay: AFT OUTLETS via EARTH LEAKAGE 1 (16A/16A), GALLEY 1 via EARTH LEAKAGE 2 (16A/16A), GALLEY 2 via EARTH LEAKAGE 3 (16A/16A).

Earth leakage relays measured on the netlist as NC-symbol relays whose measured wiring shows NO — a symbol-vs-wiring CONFLICT on all three (EARTH LEAKAGE 1, 2, 3); flagged as an uncertainty, not silently resolved.
EARTH LEAKAGE 1 (AFT OUTLETS) feeds breakers Q10-Q16 (galley outlets extractor, nav station outlets, port/stbd crew outlets, lazarette outlets, blast chiller, two spares) per net6/net7 groupings.
EARTH LEAKAGE 2 (GALLEY 1) feeds breakers Q7-Q9 (maserator, diving compressor, wine cooler galley) per net4/net5 groupings, and also appears cross-tied toward the Q1-Q6 appliance bus.

EARTH LEAKAGE 3 (GALLEY 2) feeds Q17 (induction hob, per net12/net13) and also the Q1-Q6 appliance breaker bus (oven, dishwasher, washing machine, dryer, steam oven, zip tap) — netlist shows a shared common rail (net8/net9) linking Q1, Q4, Q5, Q6 together with the dryer/steam-oven/zip-dispenser loads, indicating these six appliance breakers share a common supply rail off the Galley feeds rather than each having an independently traced private feed.
Breaker ratings as labelled: Q1 32A, Q2 25A, Q3 16A, Q4 16A, Q5 16A, Q6 16A, Q7 16A, Q8 16A, Q9 16A, Q10 16A, Q11 16A, Q12 16A, Q13 16A, Q14 16A, Q15 16A, Q16 16A, Q17 50A.

uncertainties: EARTH LEAKAGE 1, 2, and 3 relay contacts are read as NC by symbol but the measured wiring shows NO on every occurrence — a genuine symbol-vs-wiring conflict on all three earth-leakage devices; needs engineer confirmation of true contact state (does an earth-leakage trip open or close the downstream circuit).
Blast chiller (Q14) has no register node — equipment identity/placement not resolved from this sheet.

Diving compressor (Q8) attached to the general diving/watersport node (975-diving) — no more specific 'diving compressor' node exists in the register besides the Bauer brand card (970-bauer-dive-compressor); correspondence between the load name and the Bauer unit is not explicitly confirmed on this sheet.

The exact split of which appliance breakers (Q1-Q6) are fed from GALLEY 1 vs GALLEY 2 individually is not cleanly resolvable — the netlist shows a shared common rail (net8/net9) across Q1, Q4, Q5, Q6 and the dryer/steam oven/zip dispenser, suggesting a common bus rather than one dedicated earth-leakage circuit per appliance; treated as infrastructure-level fact, not per-equipment private feeds.
